findings_en:

Its inferior margin fills the posterior costophrenic angle in a wedge shape, and the anterior margin is irregular, with multiple vascular branches entering the lesion. On contrast-enhanced scans, the lesion shows gradual and persistent enhancement, becoming uniformly dense. No nodules or consolidation are seen in the right lung. No pleural effusion bilaterally.
 No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinum, bilateral hila, supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae.

findings_en: An irregular soft tissue density mass is seen around the left upper lobe bronchus, lobulated, with heterogeneous enhancement, fused with enlarged lymph nodes in stations 4L-6 of the hilum and mediastinum. The mass envelops multiple hilar vessels on the left and is closely related to the mediastinal pleura, with ill-defined margins to the peripheral lung parenchyma, measuring approximately 50 x 45 mm (IM23). Segmental bronchial narrowing and occlusion are present, with irregular patchy and linear opacities in the periphery. The remainder of both lungs shows diffuse distribution of nodules of varying sizes, the largest located in the left lung apex, measuring approximately 17 x 15 mm (IM14). An enlarged lymph node with heterogeneous enhancement is seen in the left supraclavicular region, measuring approximately 11 x 9 mm (IM5). Enlarged lymph nodes are also visible in the right hilum. The left pleura is irregular, with a small amount of effusion; the right pleura is smooth, without effusion. Pericardial thickening with effusion is present. Osseous destruction is seen in the 9th posterior ribs bilaterally, more pronounced on the left. Multiple abnormal enhancing foci are seen in the liver parenchyma.
impression_en: Irregular thickening of the bronchial wall with a peribronchial mass in the left upper lobe, malignant, with high possibility of central lung cancer, and peripheral obstructive changes. Diffuse nodules in both lungs, suggestive of metastasis. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the bilateral hila, mediastinum, and left supraclavicular region, suggestive of metastasis. Left pleural thickening with small effusion and pericardial thickening with effusion, likely metastatic. Osseous destruction in the 9th posterior ribs bilaterally, likely metastatic. Multiple hepatic metastases; correlate with abdominal imaging.

The left pleura is smooth, with a small amount of left-sided pleural effusion. A small pericardial effusion is present. Enlarged lymph nodes are visible in the right supraclavicular region, mediastinum, and right hilum, the largest measuring approximately 15x8 mm (IM27). findings_en: A large area of consolidation is seen in the left upper lobe. A soft tissue density mass measuring approximately 42x33 mm (IMA24) with low enhancement is seen at the left hilum, with invasion and narrowing of the left upper pulmonary artery and narrowing of the upper lobe bronchus. The remainder of both lungs shows emphysema. No nodules or consolidation are seen in the right lung. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes with low enhancement are seen in the 4L, 5 groups, and left hilum, with the largest measuring approximately 22x20 mm (IMA20). Bilateral pleura are smooth with no pleural effusion. No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thorax. A low-enhancing mass measuring approximately 31x28 mm (IMA65) is seen in the right adrenal gland.
impression_en:
Hilar mass in the left lung, suggestive of central lung cancer, with obstructive pneumonia in the upper lobe; bronchoscopic evaluation is recommended.
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the left hilum and mediastinum, likely metastatic.
Right adrenal mass, likely metastatic.

impression_en: Mass in the basal segment of the left lower lobe adjacent to the mediastinum, with high suspicion for malignancy, along with distal obstructive inflammation and atelectasis; further evaluation is recommended.

 Multiple ill-defined lymph nodes are seen around the bronchi of the bilateral hila, the largest measuring 22x16 mm (IM31). Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen at the lesser curvature of the stomach below the diaphragm, the largest measuring 13x9 mm (IM59).

impression_en:

 Multiple pulmonary nodules, likely representing metastases. Upper lung changes cannot exclude tuberculosis.
 Multiple enlarged hilar lymph nodes and soft tissue opacities, likely representing lymphatic metastases.
 Enlarged lymph nodes at the lesser curvature of the stomach and multiple hepatic nodules; recommend further evaluation with abdominal CT.
 Left thyroid lobe mass; recommend neck ultrasound.

Right lower lobe consolidation is present. Multiple small nodules are seen in both lungs and along the right oblique and horizontal fissures, the largest measuring approximately 7 x 7 mm (IM34).

Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen in mediastinal stations 4R, 4L, 6, and 7, the largest measuring approximately 16 x 9 mm (IM26). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the bilateral hila, supraclavicular regions, or axillae.

The left pleura is smooth; no pleural effusion is seen.

Right lower lobe mass, consistent with primary lung cancer.
Multiple small nodules in both lungs and along the right interlobar fissures, likely metastatic.
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum and right hilum, likely metastatic.
Right lower lobe consolidation, likely inflammatory; recommend follow-up.

The esophageal wall at the junction of the upper and middle thoracic segments shows irregular thickening, with a maximum thickness of approximately 14 mm (IMA26). The outer membrane is blurred, but the boundary with the descending aorta is clear. The proximal esophagus shows no dilation. Multiple lymph nodes are present in stations 1, 2, 4, 7, and 8 of the mediastinum, bilateral hilar regions, and bilateral supraclavicular areas, with the largest measuring approximately 13x11 mm (IMA32).
 A small subpleural nodule is seen in the left lower lobe, measuring approximately 2 mm (Im49). No other nodules or consolidation are seen in the remainder of the lungs.
 A small nodule is seen in the right horizontal fissure pleura (IM37). The remainder of the pleurae are smooth bilaterally, with no evidence of pleural effusion.
 No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thoracic cage within the scan range.
impression_en:
Space-occupying lesion at the junction of the upper and middle thoracic esophagus, consistent with esophageal carcinoma.
 Multiple lymph nodes in the mediastinum, bilateral hila, and bilateral supraclavicular regions, with a high possibility of metastasis.
 Small nodules in the right interlobar pleura and left lower lobe; follow-up is recommended.

Wall thickening in the distal thoracic esophagus, consistent with esophageal cancer.
 Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the paratracheal and distal esophageal regions, likely metastatic.
 Old foci in the right lung and left upper lobe.
 Tracheal diverticulum.
 Possible old fracture of the left clavicle.

 1. The extent of the soft tissue density in the anterior mediastinum is unchanged (IM18). The remainder of the mediastinum, bilateral hila, supraclavicular regions, and bilateral axillae show no enlarged lymph nodes.
 2. Status post left upper lobectomy; no abnormal soft tissue thickening is seen at the bronchial stump. The calcified focus in the right lung and punctate nodules in the left lung are unchanged (IM26), likely representing old changes. The remainder of both lungs shows no new nodules or consolidation.
 3. No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally.
 4. No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thorax within the scan range.

A large soft tissue mass is seen in the left pleural cavity, measuring approximately 96 x 88 mm in maximum cross-section (IM20), closely related to the left mediastinal vessels, pleura, and pericardium, with ill-defined tumor-lung interface; no nodules or consolidation are seen in the remainder of the lungs.
 Multiple lymph nodes are seen in mediastinal stations 3A, 6, and 5, the largest measuring approximately 26 x 17 mm (IM22). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the bilateral supraclavicular regions or axillae.
 No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally.
 No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thorax within the scan range.
impression_en:
Large mass in the left pleural cavity, suggestive of malignancy, with a higher possibility of pulmonary origin than thymic origin; biopsy recommended.
 Multiple mediastinal lymph nodes, likely metastatic.

findings_en: An oval-shaped mass is seen in the right anterior mediastinum, measuring approximately 37x24 mm (IM29). The lesion shows gradual enhancement after contrast administration, with relatively smooth margins. Adjacent vessels show no compression or deformation. No enlarged lymph nodes in the remainder of the mediastinum. No enlarged lymph nodes in the bilateral supraclavicular regions or bilateral axillae. A small nodule adjacent to the interlobar pleura in the right middle lobe measures approximately 5 mm (IM27). No abnormal density or nodules are seen in the remainder of the lungs. Both pleurae are smooth; no pleural effusion is seen. No destructive changes in the scanned bones.
impression_en: Space-occupying lesion in the right anterior mediastinum, likely of thymic origin—thymoma? Small nodule in the right middle lobe, indeterminate nature; recommend regular follow-up.

Patchy opacities are seen in the distal lower lobe. No nodules or patchy opacities are seen in the left lung.

impression_en:
Right hilar mass, likely malignant, with central lung cancer being the primary consideration.
 Patchy opacities in the right lower lobe, possibly inflammatory; correlate clinically.
 Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the right supraclavicular and mediastinal regions, likely representing metastasis.
 Right pleural and interlobar pleural thickening, possibly due to metastasis.

findings_en:
Right pleural thickening is present. Moderate pneumothorax and small pleural effusion are seen in the right pleural cavity, with compression of the right lung and a band-like area of atelectasis at the lung edge. The bronchus in the right lower lobe dorsal segment is obstructed, with an adjacent irregular soft tissue density, the largest cross-section measuring approximately 46x48 mm (IM34). The mass is poorly demarcated from the distal and surrounding atelectatic lung. The right middle lobe lung is collapsed in a mass-like fashion with heterogeneous enhancement.
 No abnormal density or nodules are seen in the left lung.
 Multiple lymph nodes are seen in mediastinal stations 4, 5, 7, and 10, the largest measuring approximately 23x17 mm (IM27). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the bilateral supraclavicular regions. The left pleura is smooth with no pleural effusion.
 No osseous destruction is seen in the visualized bones. Gas density is seen within the soft tissues of the right chest wall.
impression_en:
Right pneumohydrothorax with compression and atelectasis of the right lung.
 Bronchial cutoff in the right lower lobe dorsal segment with a mass—malignancy considered, central lung cancer likely. Multiple areas of low enhancement within the collapsed lung—recommend evaluation after re-expansion.
 Multiple mediastinal lymph nodes, some enlarged—metastasis possible?
 Subcutaneous emphysema in the right chest wall.

findings_en:

impression_en:
Wall thickening in the middle and lower thoracic esophagus, consistent with esophageal cancer.
 Small subcarinal lymph nodes visible.
 Patchy opacity in the right upper lobe apicoposterior segment; consider inflammation in clinical context; recommend follow-up.

findings_en:

Multiple lymph nodes are seen in the right supraclavicular, and mediastinal stations 2, 4, 7, and 10L, with the largest measuring approximately 42x32 mm (IMA15).
 Pulmonary markings are smooth in course; no nodules or consolidation are seen in the lungs.

impression_en:
1. Space-occupying lesion in the distal thoracic esophagus, consistent with esophageal carcinoma.
2. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the right supraclavicular and mediastinal regions, likely metastatic.

Multiple hyperdense foci are seen within, with no definite enhancement. Postoperative change? Close follow-up recommended. 
Multiple indistinct small ground-glass nodules in both lungs are similar to prior, currently measuring 3-5 mm. Linear and reticular opacities in the right middle and lower lobes are slightly decreased. 
No obvious enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum, bilateral hila, supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae.

Compared with the chest CT on [DATE]:
 Postoperative status after right middle lobectomy. The bronchial stump shows no abnormal thickening or enhancement. A cavitary nodule is seen in the left lower lobe, currently measuring approximately 12x9 mm (IM45); previously on thin-section imaging, it appeared as an irregular small nodule measuring about 6 mm, suspicious for malignancy. A new small nodule measuring approximately 2 mm is seen in the left lower lobe (IM37), to be followed. A few linear opacities are seen in the right lung; no new patchy opacities or nodules are seen.
 No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinum, bilateral supraclavicular regions, or axillae. The anterior mediastinal lymph node is slightly more prominent and denser than before, currently measuring about 9 mm (IM18), previously about 8 mm; follow-up is recommended.
 The right pleura is slightly thickened, unchanged from prior; pleural effusion is not evident. The left pleura is smooth, without pleural effusion.
 Healing callus formation is seen at the right 6th rib (Im23). No bony destruction is seen in the other bones within the scan range.

Compared with the chest CT from [DATE]: The mass in the right middle lobe has slightly increased in size, now measuring approximately 33 x 28 mm (IMA26), previously 30 x 24 mm (IMA32). Right lung atelectasis is more pronounced than before. A linear opacity is seen in the left lower lung. The multiple small nodules in both lungs are largely unchanged. The multiple small mediastinal lymph nodes are stable, with the largest measuring approximately 9 mm (IMA14). Multiple nodular thickenings are seen in the right interlobar pleura. No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally. The low-density nodule in the T10 vertebral body has increased in size and is considered possibly metastatic; recommend MRI or bone scan.
impression_en: Mass in the right middle lobe, suggestive of peripheral lung cancer. Scattered multiple small nodules in both lungs, metastasis cannot be excluded; recommend close follow-up. Multiple nodular thickenings in the right interlobar pleura, metastasis not excluded. Low-density nodule in T10, possible metastasis; recommend bone scan.

The lesion extends into the abdominal segment of the esophagus, measuring approximately 42 mm in craniocaudal extent (sagittal view, IM44). Multiple small lymph nodes are seen in the left supraclavicular region, mediastinum, and along the right lesser curvature of the cardia, with the largest measuring approximately 10 mm (IM50).
 Reticular opacities are seen in the subpleural regions of the bilateral lower lobes. No nodules or masses are seen in the lungs.
 No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally.
 No definite osseous destruction is seen in the thoracic bones.
impression_en:
Mass in the distal thoracic esophagus, suggestive of esophageal cancer.
 Multiple small lymph nodes in the left supraclavicular, mediastinal, and right cardia regions.
 Interstitial changes in both lower lobes.

Multiple lymph nodes are seen at stations 4R and 7 of the mediastinum, the largest measuring 16x7 mm (IMA28). An irregular patchy lesion is seen in the dorsal segment of the right lower lobe, measuring approximately 36 x 16 mm in cross-section (IMA30), showing marked enhancement in the delayed phase. Localized emphysema and multiple linear opacities are seen below the lesion. A round nodule is seen in the right upper lobe adjacent to the horizontal fissure, measuring approximately 6 x 5 mm (IMA29). Scattered lucencies are seen in both lungs. No nodules or consolidations are seen in the remainder of the lungs. 
 No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinum, bilateral hila, supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae. 
 The bilateral pleura are irregular, with no pleural effusion. 
 No definite osseous destruction is seen in the thoracic bones. Calcification is seen in the wall of the aortic arch.
impression_en:
Irregular patchy lesion in the right lower lobe—etiology is uncertain; lung cancer versus chronic inflammation requires further evaluation for differentiation. 
 Small pleural-based nodule in the right upper lobe—requires follow-up. 
 Scattered pulmonary bullae in both lungs.

The bronchus of the right lower lobe posterior segment is truncated. The pulmonary artery and vein of the right lower lobe posterior segment are not clearly visualized.
 A small ground-glass opacity nodule is seen in the apical segment of the right upper lobe, measuring about 3 mm (IM23).

findings_en:
Compared with the chest CT on [DATE]:

The distal right upper lobe band-like atelectasis and scattered linear and nodular opacities within the lung are unchanged. The number of scattered small nodules in both lower lobes is unchanged; some nodules are larger than before; for example, a nodule in the left lower lobe is now about 17x15 mm (IM45), previously about 13x11 mm (IM46); a nodule in the right lower lobe is now about 10x10 mm (IM41), previously about 8x6 mm (Im42). 
 2. High-density lymph nodes in the mediastinum and bilateral hila are unchanged; the largest in the right hilum is about 13x11 mm (IM29). 
 3. Aneurysmal dilation of the aortic arch and surrounding wall calcification are unchanged. 
 4. No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally.

Compared to the chest CT on [DATE]:

findings_en:
A soft tissue mass is seen around the right hilar region, measuring approximately 66 x 56 mm at its largest axial level (IM34) and about 68 mm in craniocaudal extent (coronal IM26). Enhancement is present and relatively homogeneous. The mass surrounds the right upper, middle, and lower lobe bronchi. 
 Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the right hilum and mediastinal stations 4 and 7, with the largest measuring approximately 57 x 34 mm (IM22). The right hilar mass is indistinct from the mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes. The mass is also ill-defined from the right pulmonary artery and vein, with local compression and luminal narrowing of the right pulmonary artery (IM31). Atelectasis of the right middle lobe is present. The right lower lobe bronchi show partial occlusion of the basal segments, with multiple linear and patchy opacities in the right lower lobe. No nodules or consolidations are seen in the left lung. 
 No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the left hilum, supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae. 
 A small right pleural effusion is present; no pleural effusion is seen on the left. Pericardial effusion is present. 
 The third right anterior rib shows inhomogeneous bone density (IM19). No definite destructive changes are seen in the other visualized thoracic bones.
impression_en:
Right hilar mass consistent with central lung carcinoma, with mediastinal and right hilar lymph node metastases. 
 Atelectasis of the right middle lobe; possible obstructive atelectasis with inflammation in the right lower lobe. 
 Right pleural effusion; pericardial effusion. 
 Inhomogeneous density of the third right anterior rib, indeterminate nature; further evaluation recommended.

findings_en: The right upper lobe anterior segmental bronchus shows interruption, with a large irregular soft tissue density mass visible in the lung, measuring approximately 9x7.5 cm. The periphery shows slightly higher enhancement, while the center demonstrates predominantly low enhancement. The irregular margin displays multiple spiculations of varying lengths. The inferior margin crosses the horizontal fissure pleura, causing compression and partial narrowing of the middle lobe segmental bronchi. Patchy increased density is seen in the distal upper lobe lung. Another well-circumscribed soft tissue density nodule, measuring approximately 1.2x1 cm (Im30), is seen in the right upper lobe posterior segment. A sub-centimeter irregular soft tissue density nodule is present in the left upper lobe (Im13), with relatively long surrounding spiculations. An approximately 3 cm thin-walled cavity is seen in the left lower lobe. No pleural effusion is identified bilaterally. In the mediastinum, a 4L group lymph node is enlarged, measuring approximately 1.7x1.4 cm (Im26). The 7 group shows slightly full soft tissue density. No other significantly enlarged lymph nodes are seen in other groups. The bony thoracic structure shows no obvious destructive changes.
impression_en: Right upper lobe mass crossing the horizontal fissure pleura, with high possibility of central lung cancer. The soft tissue nodule in the right upper lobe posterior segment is suggestive of a malignant focus; the left upper lobe nodule is more likely a chronic lesion; large bulla in the left lower lobe. The enlarged 4L group mediastinal lymph node raises concern for metastatic involvement; the nature of the 7 group lymph node remains indeterminate.

A soft-tissue mass is seen in the apical segment of the left upper lobe, measuring approximately 46 x 35 mm (IM14). The lesion involves the pleura at the thoracic apex and adjacent mediastinal pleura, and is closely related to the main trunk and bifurcation of the left subclavian artery, with a contact surface greater than 90°. Multiple thin-walled lucencies are seen in the subpleural regions of both lungs, more prominent in the upper lobes. Scattered linear opacities are seen in the right subpleural region. No other nodules or consolidation are seen.
 Scattered lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinal groups 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, and left supraclavicular region, the largest measuring about 14 x 9 mm (IM26).
 A small nodule is seen in the left oblique fissure pleura, measuring about 6 x 4 mm (IM40); focal thickening of the right pleura. No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally.
 Focal areas of increased density are seen in the left ribs (IM19, 35, 42); no definite osseous destruction is identified in the remainder of the thoracic cage bones.
impression_en:
Mass in the apical segment of the left upper lobe, likely malignant, involving the pleura at the thoracic apex and adjacent mediastinal pleura, and closely related to the left subclavian artery.

A rounded thick-walled cavity is seen in the posterior segment of the right lower lobe, measuring approximately 22x19 mm (IM27), with relatively uniform wall thickness and a smooth inner wall on the medial side. A few linear opacities are seen at the margin, with adjacent pleural thickening. Multiple nodules and small patchy opacities distributed along the bronchi are seen in the right lower lobe, with blurred margins; the largest is about 9x9 mm (IM23). No nodules or patchy opacities are seen elsewhere in the lungs. 
 An enlarged lymph node is seen at the right hilum, measuring approximately 18x11 mm (IM23). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinum, left hilum, bilateral axillae, or supraclavicular regions. 
 Bilateral pleura are smooth, without pleural effusion. 
 No definite bony destruction is seen in the thoracic skeleton on the scan.
impression_en:
Cavitary lesion in the posterior segment of the right lower lobe, with nodules and patchy opacities distributed along the bronchi—likely benign, tuberculosis most probable. 
 Enlarged lymph node at the right hilum—further evaluation recommended. 
 Correlate clinically and with other tests.

findings_en: A large irregular mass is seen in the left upper lobe and lingular segment, measuring approximately 69*51 mm (Fig.), with distal atelectasis observed. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen at stations 10R and 11R in the mediastinum, the largest measuring 20*14 mm (Fig. 25); no other enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes are identified. The pleura are smooth bilaterally, with a small amount of left-sided pleural effusion. No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thoracic cage. Multiple low-density nodules are seen in the bilateral thyroid glands (Fig. 8), and neck ultrasound is recommended.
impression_en: Large irregular mass in the left upper lobe and lingular segment, consistent with central left-sided lung cancer; multiple enlarged lymph nodes at the right hilum, likely representing metastasis; scattered tiny nodules in both lungs of indeterminate nature, recommend follow-up; small left-sided pleural effusion.

The mass has a broad-based contact with the oblique fissure, measuring approximately 35 mm at the interface, with adjacent pleural retraction. The mass shows marked enhancement on contrast scanning, with a net enhancement of approximately 43 HU.
 Pulmonary markings are markedly increased and disorganized bilaterally. Multiple linear opacities and honeycombing emphysema are seen in both upper lobes. No nodules or consolidation are seen in the right lung.

impression_en:

findings_en:

The fat plane between the lesion and the descending thoracic aorta is preserved. The fat plane between the esophageal lesion and the left atrium is obliterated. Cylindrical bronchiectasis is seen in the right middle lobe, lingular segment of the left upper lobe, and left lower lobe, with irregular patchy and linear opacities in the peribronchial regions. Additionally, multiple nodules are seen in the right lung, with the largest measuring approximately 19 x 14 mm (IM27). Bilateral pleural thickening is present, but no pleural effusion is seen. A small amount of pericardial effusion is present. Lymph nodes are seen in mediastinal stations 2, 3A, 4, 5, 7, 10, and 14, with the largest measuring approximately 19 x 9 mm (Im28). A small lymph node is seen in the left supraclavicular region, measuring approximately 7 mm (Im6). The T9 vertebral body shows increased density and mild flattening. A focal high-density lesion is seen in the T11 vertebral body. The superior margin of the T12 vertebral body shows mild indentation. No destructive changes are seen in the remaining bones.
impression_en:
Irregular wall thickening of the mid-to-lower thoracic esophagus, highly suggestive of esophageal carcinoma.

An irregular patchy opacity is seen adjacent to the mediastinal pleura in the right upper lobe, extending along the bronchial course, measuring approximately 27 x 24 mm on the largest axial slice (IM15), with indistinct margins. An irregular soft tissue nodule is seen in the lateral subpleural region of the right upper lobe, measuring approximately 17 x 13 mm (IM16), with indistinct margins and surrounded by multiple ill-defined patchy opacities. A small nodule is seen in the anterobasal segment of the left lower lobe, measuring approximately 5 mm (IM35), containing a calcification. The remainder of the bilateral lung markings are smooth and regularly distributed, with uniform lung lucency; no nodules or consolidation are identified.
 Several lymph nodes are seen in mediastinal stations 4–7 and the right hilum, the largest measuring approximately 12 x 6 mm (IM15). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the left hilum, bilateral supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae.
 Bilateral pleural surfaces are slightly irregular, without evidence of pleural effusion.
 No definite destructive changes are identified in the bones of the thoracic cage within the scan range.
impression_en:
Patchy opacity and soft tissue nodule in the right upper lobe, most suggestive of inflammatory change; recommend short-term follow-up after anti-inflammatory treatment to exclude malignancy.
 Small nodule in the left lower lobe, likely representing an old focus.
 Mediastinal and right hilar lymph nodes; recommend follow-up.

findings_en:
Stenosis of the right upper lobe anterior segmental bronchus, with an irregular mass surrounding it. The mass contains multiple cavities with uneven wall thickness and a ragged margin, showing small spiculations and patchy opacities. The largest cross-section measures approximately 39x32 mm (IM23). Additionally, a cavitary small nodule is seen in the right upper lobe (IM16, 34). Multiple tiny nodules are seen in the remainder of both lungs, with the largest measuring approximately 4 mm (IM48). Multiple patchy opacities are seen in the posterior basal segments of both lower lobes.
Multiple lymph nodes are present in the 4R mediastinal and right hilar regions, with the largest located at the right hilum, measuring 32x22 mm (IM23). In some sections, the boundary between this node and the mass in the right upper lobe anterior segment is indistinct. Multiple small lymph nodes are seen in the supraclavicular regions.
No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally.
No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thorax.
A non-enhancing low-density focus is seen in the liver. The medial and lateral limbs of the left adrenal gland appear thickened.
impression_en:
Mass in the right upper lobe anterior segment, consistent with lung cancer; multiple small pulmonary nodules, metastasis cannot be excluded, follow-up recommended.
Multiple lymph nodes in the mediastinum and right hilum, some enlarged, likely metastatic; follow-up recommended.
Cavitary small nodule in the right upper lobe, likely metastatic.
Multiple small lymph nodes in the supraclavicular regions.

findings_en:
Compared with the chest CT on [DATE]:
 Postoperative status of esophageal cancer. A small amount of gas and a fluid-density collection (IM9-19) adjacent to the right side of the anastomosis have increased in size. The vague, mixed slightly hyperdense sheet-like opacity in the mediastinum to the left of the intrathoracic stomach, extending from the anastomotic level to the level of the main left inferior pulmonary vein, is roughly unchanged in extent but shows decreased density; the previous non-contrast CT value exceeding 80 HU is now approximately 35 HU. Minimal pleural effusion is present bilaterally, slightly more on the left, with the right side significantly increased and locally encapsulated; internal gas has increased, with a locally honeycombed appearance. New minimal interlobar effusion is seen on the right. Atelectasis of the lower lobes is present bilaterally, more pronounced on the right. Subcutaneous emphysema in the right chest wall and neck has decreased compared to prior.
 Scattered small nodules in the left lower lobe are partially unchanged, the largest measuring approximately 4x3 mm (IM59); some are poorly visualized due to adjacent atelectasis. The nodular focus adjacent to the right horizontal fissure has increased in size, from approximately 8x3 mm (IM43) to 11x7 mm (IM38). Multiple new faint patchy opacities are seen in both lungs.
 Small lymph nodes in the left supraclavicular region are poorly visualized. No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinum, bilateral hila, right supraclavicular region, or bilateral axillae.
 No osseous destruction is seen in the thoracic skeleton.
 Diffuse atherosclerotic changes are present in the coronary arteries.
impression_en:
Postoperative status of esophageal cancer. Increased air and fluid adjacent to the anastomosis, with possible local hematoma and decreased density; anastomotic leak is possible; clinical correlation is recommended.
 Increased pneumothorax and pleural effusion on the right; clinical correlation is recommended to exclude superimposed infection. New right interlobar effusion and slightly increased left-sided effusion; worsening atelectasis; bilateral pneumonia is present; clinical correlation is recommended. Subcutaneous emphysema in the bilateral neck and right chest wall has improved.
 Scattered small nodules in the left lower lobe are partially unchanged and partially poorly visualized; follow-up is recommended.

 Small lymph nodes in the left supraclavicular region are poorly visualized; follow-up is recommended.

findings_en:
An irregular soft tissue density mass is seen in the left hilar region, fused with left hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes. The largest dimension is approximately 38x30 mm (IM27), with irregular calcification and heterogeneous enhancement of the solid component. The lesion involves and occludes the left upper lobe bronchus, with band-like atelectasis seen in the apicoposterior and anterior segments of the upper lobe. The mass encases the left pulmonary artery trunk, with irregular narrowing of the local lumen. Bronchiectasis is seen in the lateral basal segment of the left lower lobe, with a high-density nodule (Im55) and a punctate calcification adjacent to it. Multiple punctate small nodules, measuring 2-5 mm (Im28, 50, 55), are seen in the right middle and lower lobes.
 The left pleura is slightly thickened (Im28). The right pleura is smooth. No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally.
 Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen in stations 4L and 5 of the mediastinum, the largest measuring approximately 20x12 mm (IM22).
 The visualized thoracic bones show no definite destructive changes.
impression_en:
Left hilar mass, likely central lung carcinoma, with obstructive atelectasis and invasion of the left pulmonary artery trunk.
 Multiple lymph node metastases in the left hilum and mediastinum.
 Bronchiectasis with chronic changes in the left lower lobe.
 Multiple small nodules in the right lung, indeterminate; metastasis cannot be excluded; close follow-up recommended.
 Slight left pleural thickening; follow-up recommended.

Enhancement is observed on contrast scanning. Post-obstructive changes are seen in the distal lung parenchyma. Small subpleural nodules are visible in the left lower lobe and lingular segment (IM39, 43, 50, 54), the largest measuring about 6 mm. Multiple linear opacities are seen at both lung apices and near the diaphragmatic surfaces of the lower lungs. Multiple thin-walled cystic lucencies are also noted throughout both lungs.
 Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen at the right hilum, mediastinal station 7, and station 3P, the largest measuring approximately 16x8 mm (IM31). Small lymph nodes are visible in both supraclavicular regions, the largest measuring about 10x7 mm (IM6). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the left hilum or bilateral axillae.
 The pleura on both sides show mild irregular thickening. Focal thickening is seen in the interlobar pleura bilaterally. No pleural effusion is identified.
 No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thoracic cage.
impression_en:
Right lower lobe mass, suggestive of central lung cancer with involvement of the middle lobe bronchus.
 Small nodules in the left lung, likely benign; recommend follow-up. Pulmonary emphysema.
 Enlarged lymph nodes at the right hilum and mediastinum, possible metastasis. Small supraclavicular lymph nodes bilaterally, metastasis cannot be excluded.

findings_en:
An irregular soft tissue mass is seen in the apical segment of the right upper lobe, with ill-defined margins and spiculated appearance, measuring approximately 34x27 mm (IM11). A central patchy necrotic area is present with heterogeneous enhancement. The mass is closely related to the posterior pleura, with adjacent pleural thickening. The remainder of the lung parenchyma shows unremarkable bronchovascular markings and uniform lucency, without nodules or consolidation.
 An irregular cystic lesion is seen in the anterior superior mediastinum, measuring up to 35x23 mm on the largest slice (IM25), with well-defined margins and no significant enhancement. Several lymph nodes are seen at the 4R mediastinal station, the largest measuring 16x11 mm (IM22). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the remainder of the mediastinum, bilateral hila, supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae.
 The bilateral pleura are smooth, without evidence of pleural effusion.
 No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thoracic cage.
impression_en:
Mass in the apical segment of the right upper lobe, with high possibility of peripheral lung cancer, invading the pleura.
 Cystic lesion in the anterior superior mediastinum, likely cystic thymoma; recommend follow-up.
 Mediastinal lymph nodes, indeterminate nature; recommend follow-up.

findings_en: Stenosis of the right upper lobe and intermediate bronchus. The right pulmonary artery is invaded and narrowed. Scattered patchy ill-defined opacities are seen in the distal lung field of the right upper lobe. Mild interlobular septal thickening is seen in the peripheral lungs bilaterally. No nodules or consolidations are seen in the remainder of the lungs. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinal 4R, 6, and 7 stations; the one in station 6 measures approximately 20x18 mm (IMA20). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the bilateral supraclavicular regions. Bilateral pleura are smooth; no pleural effusion is seen. No definite bony destruction is seen in the scanned bones of the thorax.
impression_en: Findings consistent with central right lung cancer, with multiple lymph node metastases in the right hilum and mediastinum, and obstructive pneumonia in the right upper lobe. Mild peripheral interstitial changes in both lungs.

Multiple lymph nodes in the mediastinum, left hilum, and right lung; metastasis to be excluded, follow-up recommended. Small nodule in the left lower lobe, indeterminate; close follow-up recommended. findings_en:
Compared with chest CT on [DATE]:
 Status post right upper and dorsal segment of lower lobe resection. Sutures at the bronchial stump appear discontinuous. The large area of low enhancement surrounding the stump has decreased in size. The extent of diffuse consolidation in the right middle lobe has decreased, with multiple air cysts within. The right middle lobe artery remains unclear; the right upper pulmonary vein is thin. Multiple air and fluid collections in the right pleural cavity have slightly decreased. The chest tube is in place, entering through the anterior chest wall, coursing along the interlobar fissure, with its tip in the dorsal aspect of the right upper pleural space. Consolidation near the diaphragmatic surface of both lower lobes has improved. The tiny nodule in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe remains unchanged, measuring approximately 3 mm (IM15). Emphysema is present. Fine reticular changes in the subpleural lung markings of both lower lobes have improved.
 Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum, left hilum, and left supraclavicular region: some remain stable (e.g., mediastinal node up to 22x16 mm, IM26), while others have decreased in size (e.g., left supraclavicular node from 19x10 mm, IM5, to 15x9 mm, IM6). No enlarged lymph nodes in the right supraclavicular region or bilateral axillae. Multiple fluid-density opacities in the mediastinum have decreased.
 No pleural effusion in the left pleural cavity.
 No osseous destruction in the bones of the thorax.
impression_en:
Postoperative changes following right upper and dorsal segment of lower lobe resection. Changes at the bronchial stump and surrounding low enhancement area have decreased; multiple air-fluid collections in the right pleural cavity have slightly decreased; correlate clinically and follow-up.
 Right middle lobe consolidation has decreased in extent; persistent unclear right middle lobe artery and thin right upper pulmonary vein; partial absorption of exudate; correlate clinically and follow-up.

findings_en:
A soft tissue mass is seen in the anterosuperior mediastinum, slightly left of midline, measuring approximately 103 x 78 mm (IM21). It shows marked heterogeneous enhancement on contrast-enhanced scanning, with mild rightward displacement of the mediastinum and indistinct tumor-lung interface.
Bronchi are patent in both lungs. Scattered minor calcifications are seen in both lungs. Patchy opacities are seen in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe and basal segments of both lower lobes. No nodules or consolidation are seen in the remainder of the lungs.
Several lymph nodes are seen at the bilateral hila, the largest measuring approximately 17 x 14 mm (IM21). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinum, supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae.
Bilateral apical pleural thickening is noted. No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally.
Osseous destruction is seen in the manubrium sterni, with a soft tissue mass measuring approximately 34 x 30 mm at its largest dimension (IM11). No definite osseous destruction is seen in the remainder of the visualized thoracic bones.
Herniation of the gastroesophageal junction into the thoracic cavity is noted. A left renal cyst is present.
impression_en:
Anterior mediastinal mass, consistent with mediastinal-type lung cancer; compare with prior studies.
Osseous destruction of the manubrium sterni with soft tissue mass, likely metastatic.
Chronic pulmonary opacities and minor inflammatory changes.
Hiatal hernia.
Left renal cyst; correlate with abdominal studies.

findings_en:

findings_en:
Compared with the chest CT of [DATE]:
 Irregular wall thickening in the mid-to-lower thoracic esophagus has decreased. The maximum thickness was previously approximately 17 mm (IM32) and is now about 14 mm (IM30). Heterogeneous enhancement is still present, with blurred outer margins and increased density in the surrounding fat. The contact surface with the thoracic aorta remains less than 90 degrees. The longitudinal extent was previously about 70 mm and is now approximately 62 mm (SE401 IM36). The deformation of the left atrium has improved.
 The lymph node in the right tracheoesophageal groove has slightly increased, from approximately 13x11 mm (IM8) to 15x12 mm (IM7). Some of the multiple lymph nodes in mediastinal groups 4, 5, 7, 8, and 10 have increased in size, with the largest increasing from 18x17 mm (IM33) to 22x18 mm (IM32). The multiple small lymph nodes along the lesser curvature of the stomach have slightly decreased, with the largest reducing from 9x6 mm (IM56) to 6x5 mm (IM55).
 No abnormal densities or nodules are seen in the lungs.
 Bilateral pleura are smooth without pleural effusion.
 No destructive changes are seen in the scanned bones.
impression_en:
Post-treatment changes in mid-to-lower thoracic esophageal carcinoma, showing improvement compared to prior study.
 Multiple mediastinal lymph nodes have increased in size, while lymph nodes along the lesser curvature of the stomach have slightly decreased; recommend follow-up.

findings_en: Compared with the chest CT on [DATE]: The irregular soft tissue density mass in the left lower hilar region has decreased in size from approximately 24 mm x 10 mm to 20 mm x 10 mm (IM29). The mass involves more than 90 degrees of the descending aorta and involves the left lower pulmonary artery and vein. Multiple small subpleural nodules in both lungs are unchanged (Im27, 31, 37, 43), with irregular morphology. The left oblique fissure pleura remains slightly thickened. No pleural effusion is seen bilaterally. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the bilateral hila and mediastinal station 7 are unchanged, the largest measuring approximately 13 mm x 11 mm (IM27). No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thorax on the scan.
impression_en: Left lower hilar mass, slightly decreased in size compared to prior. Distal atelectasis has improved. Multiple lymph nodes in the bilateral hila and mediastinum are unchanged. Small nodule in the left oblique fissure pleura and multiple small nodules in both lungs are unchanged.

The margins are indistinct from the main left pulmonary artery, the left interlobar fissure, and the mediastinal pleura. A small patchy hazy opacity is seen in the anterior segment of the left upper lobe. The remainder of both lungs shows no nodules or consolidation.

Left hilar mass, likely central lung cancer, involving the left pulmonary artery and interlobar pleura, with obstructive pneumonia in the left upper lobe.
 Small left pleural effusion.

Focal irregular circumferential wall thickening is seen in the distal thoracic esophagus, with a maximum thickness of approximately 13 mm (IM44), causing luminal narrowing. The lesion shows relatively prominent enhancement in the arterial phase and decreased enhancement in the delayed phase. The boundary with the ascending aorta is well-defined. Wall thickening and enhancement are also seen from the abdominal esophagus to the cardia, with a maximum thickness of approximately 10 mm (IMA56), and a smooth outer surface. The two lesions are approximately 10 mm apart.
 Bronchi are patent in both lungs. Lung parenchyma shows uniform lucency. A calcified small nodule is seen in the right lower lobe (IM50). Scattered small nodules are seen subpleurally in the fissure of the right lower lobe (IM43, 46), the largest measuring approximately 5 mm with relatively high density. No nodules or consolidation are seen elsewhere in the lungs.
 No significantly enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinum, bilateral hila, supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae.
 Both pleural surfaces are smooth; no pleural effusion is seen.
 Small patchy hyperdense lesions are seen in the right 12th posterior rib and left 5th rib (IM17, 57). Callus formation appears to be present in the left 10th posterior rib (IM48). No definite osseous destruction is seen in the rest of the thoracic bones.
 Multiple small round non-enhancing low-density lesions and two heterogeneous enhancing masses are seen in the liver parenchyma. One enhancing nodule is seen in the medial limb of each adrenal gland.
impression_en:
1. Wall thickening in the distal thoracic esophagus and esophagogastric junction, suspicious for malignancy; correlate with endoscopy.
 2. Scattered small nodules in the right lower lobe, likely benign; requires follow-up; calcified focus in the right lower lobe.
 3. Hyperdense foci in the right 12th posterior rib and left 5th rib, likely benign; old fracture in the left 10th posterior rib? Correlate clinically.
 4. Multiple lesions in the liver and bilateral adrenal glands, likely benign; correlate with abdominal imaging.

findings_en:
Compared to the CT chest on [DATE]:
 1. Status post right pneumonectomy. No definite nodule or mass is seen at the bronchial stump. The discontinuous wall at the stump is similar to prior (IMA20), communicating with the right pleural space; the right tracheobronchial fistula remains unchanged. The smaller right hemithorax and the right pleural drainage tube are unchanged. No abnormal density is seen in the left lung.
 2. Small lymph nodes near the aortic arch, above the diaphragm, and adjacent to the thoracic aorta are partially enlarged compared to prior. The largest has increased from approximately 10x7 mm (IMA19) to 14x8 mm (IM20); close follow-up is recommended.
 3. The left pleura is smooth, with no signs of pleural effusion.
 4. No osseous destruction is seen in the bones of the thorax.

An irregular mass is seen in the right upper lobe adjacent to the mediastinum, measuring approximately 43x30 mm (IM18). The lesion has ill-defined margins with lobulation and spiculation. The apical segmental bronchus and pulmonary arterial branches of the right upper lobe enter the lesion and are truncated. The bronchial walls of the right middle and lower lobes are thickened. Multiple patchy opacities are seen in the lung, predominantly in the middle lobe, with reduced lung volume. Diffuse small nodules are seen throughout both lungs, the largest measuring approximately 12x9 mm (IM26). The right pleura is irregularly thickened.
 Multiple lymph nodes are seen in the right supraclavicular region, mediastinal stations 2, 4R, 5-8, and bilateral hila. The largest is in station 4R, measuring approximately 12x14 mm (IM17). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the left supraclavicular region or bilateral axillae. An enlarged lymph node measuring approximately 18 mm is seen below the cardia (IM52). Multiple small lymph nodes with indistinct borders are seen in the retroperitoneum.
 The left pleura is smooth, without pleural effusion.
 Focal increased density is seen in the right 4th posterior rib (IM14). No definite destructive changes are seen in the remainder of the thoracic bones.
 Hypodense nodules with ill-defined margins are seen in liver segments S4 and S6 (IM56, IM60). Multiple other hypodense nodules with well-defined margins and no enhancement are seen in the liver. A hypodense nodule is seen in the left kidney.
impression_en:
Right upper lobe mass consistent with lung adenocarcinoma.
 Diffuse nodules in both lungs are likely metastatic.
 Right middle and lower lobe atelectasis is possible—further evaluation is recommended.
 Multiple lymph nodes in the mediastinum, bilateral hila, and below the cardia are likely metastatic; multiple small retroperitoneal lymph nodes—further evaluation is recommended.
 Multiple abdominal lesions—correlation with abdominal imaging is recommended.

impression_en: Nodule in the left upper lobe, malignancy cannot be excluded; further clinical evaluation and additional studies are recommended. Enlarged left hilar lymph node; follow-up observation is advised.

findings_en: Gastric wall thickening is seen at the gastroesophageal junction, with a maximum thickness of approximately 9 mm (IM52). The outer serosal surface is relatively smooth. The lesion is primarily located in the abdominal and lower thoracic segments of the esophagus. Enlarged lymph nodes are seen near the lower esophagus and to the left of the cardia, with the largest measuring approximately 18 x 12 mm (IM50). Scattered linear and patchy opacities are seen in the right lung. A small indistinct nodule is seen in the lateral segment of the right middle lobe (IM36, 37), measuring less than 3 mm. A small linear opacity is seen subpleurally in the left lower lobe (IM40). Scattered calcified small nodules are seen subpleurally in the right lower lobe. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen in mediastinal stations 4 and 7, with the largest measuring approximately 33 x 12 mm (IM30). The nodes show high density on non-contrast imaging, with partial calcification. No enlarged lymph nodes are identified in the bilateral hila, supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae. The pleura are smooth bilaterally, without pleural effusion. The visualized thoracic osseous structures show no definite destructive changes. T9 and T10 vertebral bodies are fused. A hemangioma is seen in the T6 vertebral body (IM28). A nodular hyperdense lesion is seen within the right second rib (IM10).
impression_en: Gastric wall thickening at the gastroesophageal junction, likely malignant; correlation with endoscopy is recommended. Enlarged lymph nodes near the lower esophagus and left cardia, likely metastatic. Scattered inflammatory foci in the right lung; calcified foci in the right lower lobe. Small nodule in the right middle lobe and small linear opacity in the left lower lobe; recommend follow-up. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in mediastinal stations 4 and 7, etiology indeterminate; correlation with other relevant studies is recommended. T9 and T10 vertebral fusion; T6 vertebral hemangioma. Hyperdense nodule in the right second rib, likely a bone island; recommend follow-up.

findings_en:
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen at the right hilum, coalescing into a mass that encases the main bronchi of the right lung lobes, with marked narrowing at their origins—most pronounced in the middle lobe. The right middle lobe shows mild volume loss. A mass-like consolidation is seen at the proximal bronchus, with distal reticular and patchy opacities. Multiple hazy patchy opacities and nodular shadows are seen in the right upper lobe, with ill-defined margins; the largest measures approximately 18×14 mm (IM21). An irregular solid nodular shadow measuring approximately 28×12 mm (IM43) is seen subpleurally in the posterior basal segment of the right lower lobe, with ill-defined margins and close relationship to the pleura. Bronchovascular markings in the left lung are normal, with uniform lucency and no nodules or consolidation.
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are also seen in mediastinal stations 2R, 4R, 5, 7, and the left hilum, the largest measuring approximately 34×17 mm (IM29). An enlarged lymph node measuring approximately 30×289 mm (IM11) is seen in the left axilla. Several small lymph nodes are seen in both supraclavicular regions.
The right pleura is slightly thickened with a small amount of pleural fluid. The left pleura is smooth, without pleural effusion.
No definite destructive changes are identified in the bones of the thoracic cage within the scan range.
impression_en:
Right lung lesions are suggestive of malignancy. The nodular shadow in the posterior basal segment of the right lower lobe is likely the primary lesion, though a central bronchogenic primary cannot be excluded. The remaining lesions are likely obstructive inflammatory changes; clinical correlation is recommended.
Enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum, bilateral hila, and left axilla are suggestive of metastasis.
Small right-sided pleural effusion.

findings_en:
A soft tissue mass measuring approximately 38x17 mm is seen adjacent to the mediastinum in the right upper lobe (IM24), with irregular, lobulated margins, spiculations, and long fibrous strands, causing traction on adjacent structures. The mass surrounds and invades the right upper pulmonary vein and is closely related to the right main bronchus, with narrowing of the anterior segmental bronchus of the right upper lobe. Pulmonary markings in the remainder of both lungs are normal in course and distribution, with uniform lucency, and no nodules or consolidation.
 No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the mediastinum, bilateral hila, supraclavicular regions, or bilateral axillae.
 Mild thickening of the pleura is seen in the left lower lobe; the right pleura is smooth, with no evidence of pleural effusion.
 No definite destructive changes are seen in the bones of the thorax.
impression_en:
Post-treatment findings of central lung cancer in the right upper lobe, with invasion of the right upper pulmonary vein and narrowing of the anterior segmental bronchus of the right upper lobe; compare with prior imaging.
 Mild thickening of the left pleura, recommend follow-up.

findings_en:
There are two areas of wall thickening in the mid-lower and lower thoracic esophagus. The upper lesion is predominantly an intraluminal mass with a maximum cross-section of approximately 33 x 24 mm (IM30) and a longitudinal extent of about 9.3 cm. The lower thoracic segment shows wall thickening up to approximately 17 mm (IM55), involving about 7.2 cm, extending inferiorly into the abdominal esophagus. The cervical and upper thoracic esophagus are dilated. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the 2R/L, 4L, and 7 mediastinal groups, with the largest measuring approximately 13 x 10 mm (IM16). Multiple small lymph nodes are seen around the cardia and lesser curvature of the stomach, with the largest measuring approximately 11 x 7 mm (IM64).
 Increased and disorganized bronchovascular markings are seen bilaterally. Multiple fibrotic and calcified foci are present in the upper lungs. Hard nodules and linear bands are seen in the bilateral lower lobes, with multiple tree-in-bud nodules. Multiple bullae are seen at both lung apices. Diffuse pleural thickening and calcification are present on the right side.
 Circumferential calcification is seen in the aortic wall.
 No obvious osseous destruction is seen in the bones of the thorax.
impression_en:
Two space-occupying lesions in the mid-lower and lower thoracic esophagus, likely malignant. Multiple mediastinal lymph nodes, possibly metastatic.
 Multiple perigastric lymph nodes, metastasis cannot be excluded.
 Tuberculosis foci in both lungs, with diffuse right pleural thickening, adhesion, and calcification.

findings_en: Status post right lower lobectomy; the soft tissue at the bronchial stump is slightly thickened (IM32) without abnormal enhancement. A small nodular opacity is seen at the left lung apex, measuring approximately 3 mm (IMA10); the left pleura is smooth, without pleural effusion. Small lymph nodes are seen in the left supraclavicular region, station 7 of the mediastinum, and the right hilum, the largest measuring approximately 15 x 6 mm (IM29). No enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the bilateral axillae. The 4th and 5th right lateral ribs show increased and uneven bone density (IM24, 30), consistent with old fractures. No definite osseous destruction is seen in the rest of the visualized thoracic bones.
impression_en: Postoperative changes after right lower lobectomy. Infiltrative focus in the right upper lobe, likely inflammatory; small right pleural effusion. Small lymph nodes in the left supraclavicular region, mediastinum, and right hilum; recommend follow-up. Increased bone density in the 4th and 5th right lateral ribs, postoperative change? Recommend close follow-up.
